items.text: Oil prices surge on renewed Middle East concern: WTI +1.3% wk/wk to $81.96, Brent +4.0% to $88.90, highest since mid-June. Energy credit and refiners face margin pressure; hedging unwind and shipping cost risks escalate for speculative positions tied to energy volatility.

Labor market shows two-sided signals: July payrolls fell 23k (vs +20k prev) on weakness, yet unemployment ticked down to 4.1% and ISM Mfg employment jumped to 52.8 (expansion, first since Jan 2025). Services hiring retreated to 47.4. Uneven recovery raises default risk for temp staffing and wage-dependent credits.

Core inflation cooling but headline sticky: June CPI core 2.57% YoY (down from 2.82%), PCE core 3.29% YoY (down from 3.42%), but headline PCE 3.67% still above target. Inflation expectations easing (UMich 1-yr at 4.2% down from 4.6%). Relieves policy pressure and supports bond valuations; risk of re-acceleration on commodity shocks remains.

Fed on pause at 3.75%, ECB deposit rate steady at 2.25% post-June hike. Yield curve steepening (10y fell 6bp to 4.69%, 2y fell 3bp to 4.25%, curve widened to 46bp). Flatter rates environment benefits long-duration credit but narrows duration arbs; near-term rate cuts priced in if data softens further.

Spreads tightening modestly: HY OAS 270bp (down 3bp), IG OAS 78bp (flat), CCC OAS 1013bp (down 6bp). Low volatility (VIX 14.9, down 110bp) reflects complacency. Rising oil price and deteriorating July labor data could trigger rapid repricing; CCC cohort especially vulnerable to energy shocks and duration extension.

Macro momentum diverges: GDPNow surged to 5.83% (vs 1.54% prev, likely June base effect), while 1Q official GDP came in at 1.5%. Manufacturing PMI crushes at 55.6 (highest since May 2022), Services PMI stable at 54.1. Housing starts jumped to 1427k, existing sales declined to 4.09M. Mixed signals: strong industrial IP growth offset by cooling housing and inventory-heavy retail.

Consumer spending holds but fragile: Retail sales ex-auto +0.32% m/m in July (5.15% YoY down from 9.4% in June). UMich sentiment rebounded to 55.2 (final July, up from 49.5), but remains 11% below year-ago—inflation shadow persists. Mortgage rates at 6.69%, housing starts robust but sales down; refinancing wall and affordability stress loom for low-income borrowers.

themeCards.title: Oil Rally on Middle East Escalation
themeCards.statusLine: WTI +1.3% wk/wk, Brent +4% to $88.90, driven by renewed Iran tensions and production uncertainty. Prices remain ~$10-15 above pre-conflict baseline.
themeCards.relevance: Energy issuers face margin compression and refinancing risk; CRE and transportation credits with fuel hedges at risk. Commodity-linked loans vulnerable; spreads have not repriced; tactical short energy-collateral debt or energy-exposed issuers.

themeCards.title: Labor Market Deterioration vs. PMI Signal
themeCards.statusLine: July payroll miss (-23k) contrasts with ISM Mfg employment rebound (52.8) and strong manufacturing PMI (55.6). Services hiring turned negative (47.4). Dual narrative suggests goods-sector resilience masking broader softening.
themeCards.relevance: Conflicted signal raises recession risk if payroll decline persists; high-yield non-essential consumer and staffing credits at risk. Early default warning in wage-sensitive B/BB cohort. Monitor ADP, initial claims (199k, rising) for confirmation.

themeCards.title: CCC Cohort under Duration & Oil Pressure
themeCards.statusLine: CCC OAS at 1013bp, only 6bp tighter this week; still elevated but spreads haven't repriced higher despite labor and energy headwinds. Rates stable, issuance cooling, refinancing calendar building.
themeCards.relevance: CCC-rated energy, retail, and levered sponsors face compounding maturity walls in 2027-28. Rising oil pressure and tightening credit conditions force earlier refinancing at higher rates. Distressed mortgage origination and hospitality CCC names most vulnerable.

themeCards.title: China Manufacturing Contraction Reversal Risk
themeCards.statusLine: China NBS Mfg PMI fell to 49.2 in July (vs 50.3 June, miss 50.1), signaling renewed contraction after AI-driven rebound. Soft domestic demand and export uncertainty drive weakness.
themeCards.relevance: Chinese economy contraction spills to EM FX, commodity prices, and cross-border credit. Multinational exporters and EM-exposed corporate credit at risk; watch for Chinese sovereign spreads and interbank stress.

themeCards.title: Housing Affordability Squeeze & Refinancing Wall
themeCards.statusLine: Existing home sales fell to 4.09M (June), mortgage rates 6.69%, UMich down 11% YoY despite recent rebound. Housing starts +19% m/m but likely driven by pent demand and seasonal factors, not demand elasticity.
themeCards.relevance: Tight affordability locks out marginal borrowers; ARM reset calendar concentrated 2026-27. Alt-A/No-Doc portfolio and non-QM lenders facing delinquency acceleration. Subordinate MBS and home-builder credits vulnerable; watch for builder margin compression.

themeCards.title: Retail Momentum Deceleration Post-Prime Day
themeCards.statusLine: July retail sales +5.15% YoY ex-auto (core down from 10%+ in June); m/m +0.32% (slowest in months). Promotional intensity and tariff pull-forward peaked; inventory levels normalizing post-summer.
themeCards.relevance: Discretionary retail credits (apparel, furniture, e-commerce) face margin pressure and slowing demand. Specialty retailer debt and high-beta discretionary issuers at downgrade risk if delinquency trends deteriorate or same-store sales flatten into H2.

regime.detail: Manufacturing resilience masks labor softness; inflation cooling but energy shock resurging; tight spreads, rate pause, housing affordability cracking
